findings.title: Cancellation can win after the final pre-dispatch check yet the configuration adapter is still invoked
Batch cleanup did not recheck an external writer after taking the HOME lease
Cancellation racing a pre-spawn adapter failure can revoke the captured admission certificate
Credential or dependency rotation during failure cannot redirect revocation from the captured scope
Preflight rejection without a captured verification reference preserves a newer certificate
Concurrent proposal completion returns a coherent state and payload snapshot
A native transcript change before the batch lease is detected and aborts all cleanup side effects

limitations: I independently reconstructed the candidate manifest: all 203 entries produce candidate SHA-256 b8b195e38348d5dc2e35c2d533a8c16f1af28e9b51b366327b0fbfba1e80a092. I also verified all 201 entries in the sealed r11 evidence manifest by size and SHA-256. The contract hash and declared Git tree 413170e6cdcbcb370a3c4347c4b29dd06f2d45f7 match the supplied identity.

The substantive three-file dispatch change closes the prior adapter-spawn issue. `_claim_dispatch` serializes cancellation against the durable CONFIGURATION_DISPATCH claim; ConfigurationJournal atomically rejects cancellation at AGENT_REQUEST and PROCESS intent; and the native process loop stops an owned process before further stdin. My scratch-only rerun of all seven shipped AtomicConfigurationDispatchTests passed. The sealed focused verification also records separate-store SQLite exclusion, rejected AGENT_REQUEST/PROCESS intents with zero spawn calls, no replay, cancellation of an owned child, and captured-record CAS behavior.

A distinct remaining race is reproducible in the current source. In `tools/studio/configuration_assistant.py:175-177`, the exception path reads `cancel_requested` outside the certificate transaction, then decides whether to call `ModelAdmission.invalidate`. A cancellation writer can commit after that read but before `invalidate`. My bounded scratch-only test made CLI.start fail before AGENT_REQUEST or PROCESS intent, returned the old false cancellation snapshot to that catch path, then committed cancellation through a separate Storage connection. The operation correctly became CANCELLED with no proposal fields and only CONFIGURATION_DISPATCH recorded, but the previously VERIFIED certificate became FAILED. Thus no native process had started, yet cancelled pre-spawn failure did not preserve the certificate. This contradicts the stated cancellation safety property and keeps SC06 and SC09 failed.

This is not the former final-read-to-CLI TOCTOU: the new reproduction does not claim a provider process was spawned after cancellation. It is a separate exception-path ordering flaw caused by deriving the invalidate decision from a stale cancellation read. The existing optional renewal guard and final publication transaction do not cover this path.

I inspected, rather than re-ran, the sealed current broad evidence: 722 Python tests, 6 host tests, 56 editor/projection JS tests, 191 ordinary HTTP/Chromium checks, baseline, syntax, rebuild, privacy, current AI-configuration journey, model catalog registration, same-UUID native chat/terminal evidence, and the fixed-runner implementation verification. The sealed records report no failures. No model call, authentication read, source write, authority write, Git operation, Stable operation, or external publication was performed in this review.

The original SC04 batch-writer finding remains closed: current bounded and sealed tests cover post-lease external writer detection, fixed membership/version, post-scan native identity change, queued writers, and own-held lease behavior. The reported ordinary browser interruption in earlier r10 history remains unexplained; r11's later complete ordinary browser record was inspected as evidence, not represented as a new source explanation.

Real records support the required model-directory configuration, configuration generation/application, workflow sequence, and same-UUID native Codex/Claude Q/A claims. Physical backend identity and effective effort remain unknown. Registration remains distinct from execution admission; applying a configuration proposal remains draft-only; Agent-mode future workspace-write remains a request requiring separate runtime consent.

The old Task03 limited accepts and old Gate BLOCKED records remain historical only. This review makes no formal technical acceptance, user-experience acceptance, main merge, Stable promotion, or current Gate claim.
